{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABWCSegw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6Pzg_k8ak", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 35, "title": "Implement PMX UV and additional UV morphs in TSL, with group/VMD playback and private viewer", "body": "## Goal

Implement **PMX type 3 UV morph** and **type 4–7 additional UV1–4 morphs** in `three-mmd-loader` using the existing Three.js r186 TSL / NodeMaterial render paths, including named VMD morph tracks, direct interactive weights, and direct PMX type 0 group links. Preserve compatibility with the already-implemented vertex, SDEF, bone, group and material morphs.

## Verified current baseline

- `MMDLoader.GeometryBuilder` currently contains **TODO** branches for PMX morph types 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. Base `uv` (vec2) is exposed, but `PmxVertex.auvs` are not built into runtime GPU attributes.
- Public `mmd-parser@1.1.4` already parses types **3–7** as `{ index, uv: [x,y,z,w] }` and preserves `PmxVertex.auvs` (up to four vec4 channels). Its current `leftToRightModel` does **not** spatially flip UV offsets. No parser release should be needed unless tests demonstrate a concrete parser defect.
- Direct type 0 group links for vertex/bone/material are implemented, while group→UV is currently unsupported.
- `MMDToonMaterial` samples color maps in TSL, uses view-derived coordinates for sphere/toon effects, and has a separate alpha-aware shadow path. Existing SDEF attributes share an interleaved GPU vertex buffer to respect WebGPU vertex-buffer limits.

## Functional scope

1. **Base UV morph (type 3).** Apply the weighted UV0 offset to the sampled `uv` coordinates of actual `MMDLoader` meshes, not merely preserve metadata. Use `uv.xy` for standard vec2 texture sampling; retain all four PMX offset components for inspection and distinguish the unused z/w values. Ensure diffuse/color-map and related UV0-dependent alpha/depth/shadow sampling use the same effective UV; do **not** accidentally shift view-based sphere mapping or lighting-coordinate toon sampling.
2. **Additional UV1–4 morphs (types 4–7).** Preserve each declared extra UV base channel as a **vec4**, and apply the corresponding per-vertex vec4 morph offsets. Define documented, public **TSL/node-accessible** names or an equivalent typed API allowing application shaders to use the *morphed* extra UV channels; verify all four components (not only xy). Do not claim ordinary built-in MMD materials automatically display extra UVs when no shader consumes them. When a channel is absent, behavior must be explicit, finite and non-crashing. Do not create nonexistent channels merely because a morph references them.
3. **Weights and groups.** Keep original names, indices and `morphTargetDictionary` / `morphTargetInfluences` stable. Each effective target weight is direct weight plus contributions `groupWeight × elementRatio` from valid direct type 0 links; preserve existing documented semantics (nested group references ignored, duplicates/shared targets summed without clamping) and existing vertex/bone/material behavior. Prevent accidental double application between Three built-in morph handling and custom UV evaluation.
4. **Animation and lifecycle.** Integrate with `MMDAnimationHelper`, default mode and `pmxAnimation: true`. Static slider changes followed by `helper.update(0)`, VMD tracks, paused/stopped playback, seek, loops, reset and helper transfers must restore baseline/avoid accumulated offsets or stale GPU data. If UV evaluation is shader-driven, explicitly document whether `helper.update(0)` is required and retain predictable values in non-animated renders.
5. **Coordinate/texture conventions.** Assert base UV and offset signs, texture origin/V orientation, `Texture.flipY`, rendering and sampling correctness using deliberately asymmetric UV deltas and a non-symmetric colored texture. Do not transpose/negate channels or reinterpret PMX vec4 UV deltas as positions. Verify shader UV0 use in the standard material and the shadow/alpha path; document texture sampling and wrapper/clamp behavior as relevant.
6. **Performance and backend portability.** Work in actual TSL on mandatory WebGL2 and native WebGPU when available, without custom GLSL/WGSL forks. Respect Three r186 vertex attribute/buffer limits (especially mixed SDEF meshes, normal, tangent and four additional UV channels); consider interleaved attributes/selective attribute exposure or another tested viable representation. Keep original mesh data intact, avoid unnecessary per-frame reallocations and document scalability limitations.
7. **Exclusions.** PMX 2.1 flip/impulse morphs, custom MME shader behavior and arbitrary material effects driven by extra UVs, sphere-map mode `envFlag=3`, full Grant fixes, and changes to published examples are **not** part of this Issue.

## Optional local real-model verification

**Candidate: ワイヤーロープ (Wire Rope) by まりりん** — original distribution https://bowlroll.net/file/69264. Creator description reports an interaction between **bone morphs and UV morphs**; it was also a candidate for completed bone-morph Issue #28. This is a **candidate only**: no PMX bytes have been inspected to prove its actual morph type numbers, values or required usage.

- Extend the existing loopback-only `npm run dev:sdef` viewer with **uv-morph/** selection under Git-ignored `examples/assets/private/uv-morph/`; preserve previous SDEF/bone/group/material viewer functionality. Alternatively allow the already-private bone-morph directory for the same model without copying or exposing assets.
- Show actual type 3–7 morph names, indices, nonzero element counts, target vertex IDs, channel numbers, xyz/w offsets, linked group names/ratios and base/morphed UV diagnostics. Provide independent 0 → 0.5 → 1 → 0 sliders for direct and group weights; allow optional licensed VMD playback and reset.
- Provide a **local generated** checker-texture test case, or a togglable UV visualization shader, so a clearly visible UV0 shift can be distinguished from missing/unused additional-UV shader consumption.
- Read the downloaded model's actual README/license before local use; do not acquire, upload, commit, redistribute or deploy third-party PMX/texture/VMD assets automatically, nor assume permission to publish. Existing public examples/assets/screenshots/URLs and Pages manifests remain untouched.
- Real-model visual inspection is informative and **not** a merge prerequisite. [Issue #30](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/30) remains an independent deferred human check and must not be closed as a side effect.

## Fully automated pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Synthetic PMX fixtures through public `mmd-parser@1.1.4` cover nontrivial UV0 and 1–4 additional UV bases, type 3–7 morph elements and different declared additional-UV counts (including 0), malformed/out-of-range indices, nonfinite weights, duplicate elements and direct + group interactions. All original morph names/indices remain stable.
- [ ] Independent CPU reference compares effective `uv.xy` and each additional-UV `xyzw` against baseline + weighted sums (including negative/fractional/over-one values), at weights 0/0.5/1, and after reset. Tests distinguish sign/flipped-V and accidental vec4-to-vec2 truncation.
- [ ] Group→type 3–7 works with the same reference arithmetic as direct morphs; nested groups remain ignored and valid non-UV group targets stay functional without double application.
- [ ] Actual browser **texture pixel/readback** tests demonstrate base UV morph effects on `MMDToonMaterial` color-map sampling and alpha/shadow consistency using asymmetric textures and UV coordinates; additional UV1–4 get separate actual TSL GPU-readback tests of all four components using a custom test shader. Do not mistake the absence of a default consumer for a broken additional-UV morph.
- [ ] Mandatory WebGL2 and native WebGPU when available are exercised against independent expected results for at least one mesh mixing SDEF, other bone skinning, vertex morph and UV morphs. Stress the four-channel attribute/vertex-buffer limit rather than merely compiling an empty shader.
- [ ] VMD named morph tracks, static slider updates, paused/stopped/seek/loop/reset and both helper modes are deterministic. No accumulating UV deformation or corruption of unaffected morph/material/SDEF state across multiple frames and helper transfers.
- [ ] Invalid indices/nonfinite values are safely handled and do not corrupt draw state, matching existing robustness conventions. Existing PMD/PMX loading and non-morph UV rendering remain unchanged.
- [ ] Private viewer demonstrates real PMX type 3–7 diagnostics when supplied locally and can run with generated fixtures alone. Security/packaging tests keep model files and viewer excluded from npm packs, public builds, Pages, and CI artifacts.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run build:examples`, `npm run test:examples`, and isolated npm JS/TS consumer tests all pass **before merge**.
- [ ] No third-party download, human visual signoff, credentialed access, or post-merge site checks are needed for Issue/PR completion.

## Required post-merge verification

**None** for implementation Issue/PR completion. Optional human real-model inspection and any future public model replacement are separate processes.
